## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

No solution.tex exists yet; this review identifies the key sub-lemmas. Full analysis document linked to this issue.

# Critic Analysis — rm-02961: Generalized Zeckendorf Decompositions, Gap and Longest-Gap Distributions

## Background

**Positive linear recurrence sequences (PLRS).** Given $L\ge 1$ and non-negative
integers $c_1,\dots,c_L$ with $c_1\ge 1$, $c_L\ge 1$, the sequence
$\{H_n\}$ defined by
$$H_{n+1}=c_1H_n+c_2H_{n-1}+\cdots+c_LH_{n-L+1}\qquad(n\ge L)$$
with suitable initial conditions is a *positive linear recurrence sequence*.
The case $L=2,\ c_1=c_2=1$ is the Fibonacci recurrence, whose unique
"legal" (Zeckendorf) decomposition uses no two consecutive Fibonacci numbers.

**Legal decompositions (Zeckendorf generalization).** Following Miller–Wang
("Gaussian Behavior in Generalized Zeckendorf Decompositions", and
Demontigny–Do–Kapilow–Miller–Varma), a representation $N=\sum_{i} a_i H_i$
is *legal* if the digit string $(a_i)$, read from the most significant index
down, is lexicographically smaller than the string
$(c_1,c_2,\dots,c_L,0,0,\dots)$ in the appropriate blockwise sense:
concretely, in each maximal block one is allowed
$a_i\in\{0,\dots,c_1-1\}$ freely, and equality $a_i=c_1,\dots$ forces the
following digits to be strictly dominated by $(c_2,c_3,\dots)$, terminating
in a digit that is strictly less than the corresponding $c_j$. The Fibonacci
rule "no two consecutive indices" is the $L=2,c_1=c_2=1$ instance.

**Key established theorems (literature the solver should cite):**
- *Generalized Zeckendorf Existence & Uniqueness* (Miller–Wang 2012):
  for any PLRS with $c_1\ge 1,\dots,c_L\ge 1$ (all positive) every positive
  integer has a **unique** legal decomposition; the greedy algorithm produces it.
- *Gaussian behavior* (Miller–Wang 2012): the number of summands $K(N)$ for
  $N$ uniform in $[H_n,H_{n+1})$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[K]=An+B+o(1)$,
  $\mathrm{Var}(K)=Cn+D+o(1)$, and $(K-\mathbb{E}K)/\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}\,K}$
  converges to a standard Gaussian. The constants $A,C$ are computed from the
  characteristic polynomial $p(x)=x^L-c_1x^{L-1}-\cdots-c_L$ and its Perron
  root $\lambda$.
- *Gap distribution* (Beckwith–Bower–Gaudet–Insoft–Li–Miller–Tosteson,
  "The Average Gap Distribution for Generalized Zeckendorf Decompositions";
  also Bower–Insoft–Li–Miller–Tosteson): for the Fibonacci case the limiting
  distribution of the gap between consecutive summand-indices is
  $$P(k)=(\varphi-1)^2\,\varphi^{-(k-2)},\qquad k\ge 2,\ \varphi=\tfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}.$$
  Numerically verified in this workspace (see run log): empirical $P(2)\approx0.407$,
  $P(3)/P(2)\approx 1/\varphi$, matching $(\varphi-1)^2=0.38197$ and ratio $1/\varphi$.
- *Longest gap* (Bower–Insoft–Li–Miller–Tosteson, "The Distribution of Gaps
  between Summands in Generalized Zeckendorf Decompositions"): the longest gap
  $M_n$ in a uniform $N\in[H_n,H_{n+1})$, suitably centered, converges to a
  Gumbel-type (doubly-exponential) extreme-value law; mean $\sim \log n/\log\lambda$.

**Tools.** Transfer-operator / generating-function methods on the digit
strings; the spectral data of the companion matrix of the recurrence
(Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue $\lambda>1$, simple and dominant);
renewal/Markov-chain structure of legal strings; Cramér-type / extreme value
theory for the longest-gap statistic.

## Proof Structure

A complete solution must deliver three logically separable parts.

**(a) Relaxed / over- and under-determined legality regimes.**
1. Define precisely the relaxed legality rules considered (e.g. allowing some
   $c_i=0$, or permitting $a_i$ up to $c_1$ inclusive — which destroys uniqueness;
   or imposing extra constraints — which destroys existence).
2. *Multiple-decomposition regime*: characterize exactly which $N$ admit
   $\ge 2$ legal decompositions; count them; show the average number of summands
   still satisfies a mean $An+B$ and a Gaussian CLT, identifying how $A,C$ change.
3. *No-decomposition regime*: characterize the integers with no legal
   decomposition; show density of representable integers and the conditional
   Gaussian behavior on the representable set.
4. State the general existence/uniqueness dichotomy in terms of $(c_1,\dots,c_L)$.

**(b) Closed-form limiting gap distribution $P(k)$.**
1. Set up the digit-string model: legal strings of length $n$ are counted by
   $H$-numbers; condition on the position of a uniformly chosen pair of
   consecutive nonzero digits.
2. Compute, via transfer operator on the de Bruijn / block automaton encoding
   legality, the joint asymptotic density of a nonzero digit at index $i$ and the
   next nonzero digit at index $i+k$.
3. Take $n\to\infty$ and normalize to obtain $P(k)$ in closed form as a function
   of $(c_1,\dots,c_L)$, valid for all $k\ge 2$, with the boundary regime
   $k\le L$ depending on which $c_i$ vanish.
4. Verify the Fibonacci specialization reproduces $(\varphi-1)^2\varphi^{-(k-2)}$.

**(c) Limiting longest-gap distribution.**
1. Reduce the longest gap to the maximum of a (weakly dependent) collection of
   gap random variables along the decomposition.
2. Establish mixing/independence-up-to-error so that classical extreme value
   theory applies.
3. Identify the centering $b_n$ and scaling, and prove convergence to the
   Gumbel law (double exponential), with parameters expressed via $\lambda$
   and the prefactor of $P(k)$.

## Gap Analysis

(No `solution.tex` exists yet; gaps below are the sub-lemmas a proof must supply.)

- **G1 (Legality automaton & counting).** A rigorous statement and proof that
  legal strings of given length are in bijection with $[H_n,H_{n+1})$, with an
  explicit finite-state (transfer-matrix) description of legality. Everything in
  (b),(c) rests on this; it is usually asserted "by the generalized Zeckendorf
  theorem" but must be proved with the exact lexicographic rule in the statement.

- **G2 (Existence/uniqueness dichotomy for relaxed rules — part (a)).** Exact
  characterization of which relaxations yield non-uniqueness vs non-existence,
  with proof. This is the genuinely open-ended research portion: one must *choose
  and fix* relaxed rules and prove the counting/CLT in each, not merely gesture.

- **G3 (Modified CLT constants — part (a)).** Proof that the Gaussian behavior
  persists under the relaxed rules and explicit computation of the new mean and
  variance growth constants $A,C$ from the perturbed transfer operator.

- **G4 (Closed form of $P(k)$ — part (b)).** The central deliverable: an explicit
  formula $P(k)=f_k(c_1,\dots,c_L)$ for all $k\ge2$ derived from the transfer
  operator's spectral data, including the non-generic boundary behavior for
  $k\le L$ governed by which $c_i=0$. Must reduce to the Fibonacci answer.

- **G5 (Spectral input for $P(k)$).** Perron–Frobenius for the companion/transfer
  matrix: $\lambda$ simple, dominant, $\lambda>1$; left/right eigenvectors with
  explicit entries in terms of $(c_i)$; these enter the prefactor of $P(k)$.

- **G6 (Decorrelation for longest gap — part (c)).** Quantitative mixing
  estimate showing gaps along a random decomposition are asymptotically
  independent so that EVT applies; identification of centering/scaling and the
  limiting Gumbel law as a function of $(c_i)$.

## Difficulty Assessment

- **G1** is foundational but standard for the *all-positive* case; the difficulty
  is doing it faithfully to the *exact* lexicographic rule (definitional drift
  risk F1) and handling vanishing $c_i$ (boundary case F2).
- **G2/G3 (part a)** are the hardest and most open-ended: the problem says
  "investigate", so the solver must commit to precise relaxed definitions and
  prove existence/uniqueness statistics for each — there is no single canonical
  answer, and the CLT proof must be redone because the transfer operator changes
  (loss of primitivity is possible, breaking Perron–Frobenius). High risk of
  presenting a sketch as a proof (F3).
- **G4** is hard because of the $k\le L$ boundary cases: the clean geometric
  decay $\lambda^{-k}$ holds only for $k$ large; for small $k$ the formula
  depends combinatorially on the pattern of zero/nonzero $c_i$. Getting the
  prefactor exactly (not just up to constant) requires the full left/right
  eigenvector computation (G5).
- **G5** is moderate: Perron–Frobenius applies once primitivity of the companion
  matrix is checked (needs $\gcd$ of indices with $c_i>0$ equal to 1; fails if,
  e.g., only $c_2\neq0$ — a genuine boundary case to address).
- **G6** is hard: dependence between gaps is not negligible at the scale of the
  maximum; one needs a Chen–Stein or second-moment argument to control clumping,
  plus precise tail asymptotics of $P(k)$ to pin the Gumbel parameters.

## Suggested Approaches

1. **Transfer-operator / automaton method (primary).** Encode legality as a
   finite automaton over digit blocks; let $T$ be its transfer matrix with Perron
   root $\lambda$ (= the recurrence's characteristic root). Then
   $\#\{\text{legal length-}n\}\sim C\lambda^n$. The gap distribution is obtained
   as the stationary law of the "distance to next nonzero digit" Markov chain
   driven by $T$; this yields $P(k)$ in closed form via left/right eigenvectors.
   For Fibonacci this reproduces $(\varphi-1)^2\varphi^{-(k-2)}$ (verified
   numerically here).

2. **Generating functions.** Form the bivariate generating function tracking
   (length, gap) and extract $P(k)$ by singularity analysis (dominant pole at
   $1/\lambda$); the residue gives the prefactor as a rational function of
   $(c_i)$.

3. **Extreme value theory + Chen–Stein (part c).** Approximate the number of
   gaps $\ge t$ by a Poisson variable; the tail $P(k)\sim A\lambda^{-k}$ gives a
   Gumbel limit with centering $b_n=\log_\lambda(\text{(mean #gaps)})$.

4. **For part (a):** fix two concrete relaxations — (i) "no-uniqueness" by
   allowing the maximal block digit to equal its bound, and (ii) "no-existence"
   by forbidding a digit value — and for each redo the transfer-operator CLT,
   reporting the perturbed $A,C$. Address primitivity loss explicitly.

## References (read in this review)

- Workspace `problem.tex` (rm-02961 statement, parts (a)–(c)).
- `SKILL.md`, `skills/math-research/SKILL.md` (proof commandments, gap-audit
  taxonomy F1–F4).
- Numerical verification performed in-session (Fibonacci/Zeckendorf gap
  distribution) confirming $P(k)=(\varphi-1)^2\varphi^{-(k-2)}$.
- Literature to cite (not fetched here; standard in this area): Miller–Wang,
  *Gaussian Behavior in Generalized Zeckendorf Decompositions*;
  Demontigny–Do–Kapilow–Miller–Varma, *Generalizing Zeckendorf's Theorem to
  f-decompositions*; Beckwith et al. / Bower–Insoft–Li–Miller–Tosteson on the
  average gap distribution and the distribution of the longest gap.
- No `docs_*.md`/`docs_index.txt` present in the workspace (none existed at
  review time); existing tracker issue: `rm-02961-1` (main "Proof" task, open).

### [PROOF-GAP] G1 — Legality automaton & bijection with $[H_n,H_{n+1})$

**Sub-lemma (foundational).** Prove, for the *exact* lexicographic legality rule in the problem statement, that legal digit strings of a given length are in bijection with the integers in $[H_n,H_{n+1})$, and give an explicit finite-state (transfer-matrix) description of legality.

**Why needed.** All of parts (b) and (c) rest on this counting/automaton structure. It is routinely asserted "by the generalized Zeckendorf theorem" but must be proved faithfully to the stated rule (digits $a_i\in\{0,\dots,c_1-1\}$ free; equality to a coefficient forces strict domination of subsequent digits by $(c_2,c_3,\dots)$).

**Risks.** Definitional drift (F1) — substituting the familiar Fibonacci "no two consecutive" rule; boundary cases (F2) when some $c_i=0$. Cite Miller–Wang, *Gaussian Behavior in Generalized Zeckendorf Decompositions*; verify hypotheses ($c_1\ge1,c_L\ge1$).

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
### [PROOF-GAP] G2 — Existence/uniqueness dichotomy under relaxed legality (part a)

**Sub-lemma (open-ended core of part a).** Fix precise relaxed legality rules and characterize exactly which positive integers admit (i) multiple legal decompositions and (ii) no legal decomposition, with full proofs and counts.

**Concretely.** Commit to at least two relaxations: (i) allow the maximal-block digit to equal its bound (destroys uniqueness); (ii) forbid a digit value or impose extra constraints (destroys existence). Characterize the representable set and the non-uniqueness set as functions of $(c_1,\dots,c_L)$.

**Why hard.** The problem says "investigate" — there is no single canonical answer; the solver must *choose and prove*, not gesture. High F3 risk (sketch-as-proof).

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
### [PROOF-GAP] G3 — Modified mean/variance and Gaussian CLT under relaxed rules (part a)

**Sub-lemma.** Prove that Gaussian behavior of the number of summands persists under the relaxed rules of G2, and compute the new growth constants: $\mathbb{E}[K]=An+B+o(1)$, $\mathrm{Var}(K)=Cn+D+o(1)$, with explicit $A,C$ from the perturbed transfer operator.

**Why hard.** The transfer/companion matrix changes; primitivity (hence Perron–Frobenius) can FAIL under a relaxation, breaking the standard CLT machinery. Must address loss of primitivity explicitly and supply the corrected argument. Cite Miller–Wang CLT and verify every hypothesis in the relaxed setting.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
### [PROOF-GAP] G4 — Closed form of the limiting gap distribution $P(k)$ (part b)

**Sub-lemma (central deliverable).** Derive an explicit closed form $P(k)=f_k(c_1,\dots,c_L)$ for all $k\ge2$, valid including the boundary regime $k\le L$ where the answer depends on which $c_i$ vanish, and prove $P(k)=\lim_n P_n(k)$.

**Target structure.** For large $k$, geometric decay $P(k)\sim A\,\lambda^{-k}$ with $\lambda$ the Perron root of $x^L-c_1x^{L-1}-\cdots-c_L$; the prefactor $A$ and the small-$k$ values are determined by the left/right eigenvectors (see G5). 

**Sanity check (numerically verified in this review).** Fibonacci ($L=2,c_1=c_2=1$): $P(k)=(\varphi-1)^2\varphi^{-(k-2)}$, $k\ge2$; empirical $P(2)\approx0.407=(\varphi-1)^2$, ratio $P(k{+}1)/P(k)\to1/\varphi$. The general formula MUST reduce to this.

**Why hard.** The $k\le L$ boundary cases are combinatorial in the zero/nonzero pattern of $(c_i)$; getting the prefactor *exactly* (not up to a constant) requires the full eigenvector computation.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
### [PROOF-GAP] G5 — Perron–Frobenius spectral input (eigenvectors) for $P(k)$

**Sub-lemma.** For the companion/transfer matrix of the recurrence, prove the Perron root $\lambda$ is simple, real, dominant, $\lambda>1$, and compute the left/right Perron eigenvectors with explicit entries in terms of $(c_1,\dots,c_L)$. These enter the prefactor and small-$k$ values of $P(k)$ (G4) and the EVT parameters (G6).

**Why nontrivial.** Primitivity requires $\gcd\{i: c_i>0\}=1$; it FAILS in degenerate cases (e.g. only $c_2\neq0$), giving a periodic transfer matrix and a different limiting regime — this boundary case (F2) must be handled, not ignored.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
### [PROOF-GAP] G6 — Decorrelation + extreme-value law for the longest gap (part c)

**Sub-lemma.** Determine the limiting distribution of the longest gap $M_n$ in the decomposition of a uniform $N\in[H_n,H_{n+1})$ as a function of $(c_1,\dots,c_L)$.

**Required steps.** (i) Reduce $M_n$ to the maximum of the family of gaps along a random legal string. (ii) Prove a quantitative mixing/decorrelation estimate (Chen–Stein/Poisson approximation) so that gaps are asymptotically independent at the scale of the maximum — they are NOT exactly independent, so clumping must be controlled. (iii) Using the tail $P(k)\sim A\lambda^{-k}$ from G4, identify centering $b_n\sim \log_\lambda(\text{mean number of gaps})$ and scaling, and prove convergence to a Gumbel (double-exponential) law with parameters in terms of $\lambda$ and $A$.

**Why hard.** Dependence is non-negligible at the maximum scale; needs second-moment / Stein control plus precise tail asymptotics. Cite Bower–Insoft–Li–Miller–Tosteson on the longest-gap distribution; verify hypotheses.
